# Intent — writing `intent.md` the organization's way

You are writing `projects/<PRJ>/intents/<NN-slug>/intent.md`. Below is what the organization's lifecycle says about this step, the sections the
artifact must carry, and its template. The lifecycle policy is the authority; this is a copy of it.

## What the lifecycle says — Intent

Template: `policies/reference/lifecycles/ai-sdlc/intent.md`

- An intent is made from one or more board issues. Related issues may be grouped into one intent.
- The owner interview: the agent drafts the intent from the issues, then interviews the business owner one
  question at a time, each with a recommendation, asking only what the record does not already answer —
  outcome, who benefits, priority, success measure, what is in and out of scope, constraints and risks.
- The business owner approves the result. An intent written without the interview stays DRAFT.

## What `intent.md` must carry

Open with the template's front matter and the Status line `**Status:** DRAFT`. You never write APPROVED: gov
writes it when a person approves the change request and it merges.

Then every one of these sections, as a `##` heading, in this order:

- Goal
- Why
- Board items
- Rulings it carries
- Affected units
- Interview decisions
- Out
- Done when

## The template — `policies/reference/lifecycles/ai-sdlc/intent.md`

````markdown
---
domain: development
layer: spec
owner: <owner>
compliance: C01
status: draft
---

# Intent <NN>: <title>

**Status:** DRAFT
<!-- One of: DRAFT · APPROVED by <who> <date> (<change request link>) · STALE (<why>).
     gov writes the APPROVED line when the change request is approved by a person and merged; never write it by hand. -->

**Project:** <PRJ> · **Template:** `policies/reference/lifecycles/ai-sdlc/intent.md`

## Goal
<What will be true for the business when this is done, in one or two sentences.>

## Why
<The problem or opportunity, and who feels it.>

## Board items
- <issue link> <title>

## Rulings it carries
<Decisions already made elsewhere that this intent must honour, or "none".>

## Affected units
<Which deployable units change.>

## Interview decisions
<!-- The owner interview: one question at a time, each with a recommendation, asking only what the record does
     not answer — outcome, who benefits, priority, success measure, in/out of scope, constraints, risks. -->
- **Q1** <question> → <answer> (<who>, <date>)

## Out
<What this intent will not do.>

## Done when
<The observable result that says the intent is met.>
````
